title: "SSH vs HTTPS"

# SSH vs HTTPS

After this page you can authenticate to a forge over SSH or HTTPS and know which URL form you are looking at.

## Two ways to talk to a remote

| | SSH | HTTPS |
|--|-----|-------|
| URL | `git@host:owner/repo.git` | `https://host/owner/repo.git` |
| Secret | Private key on disk | Password, personal access token, or credential helper |
| Typical use | Daily push/fetch on a machine you own | CI, quick clone, hosts that block SSH |

Both speak the Git smart protocol. The difference is how the server decides who you are. Part I does not require a forge. Set this up before chapter 11 so the first push is not a scavenger hunt.

```text
  Linux laptop                         forge
 ┌──────────────────┐                 ┌──────────────────┐
 │ ~/.ssh/id_ed25519│  SSH            │ authorized keys  │
 │   (private)      │ ──────────────► │ git@host         │
 │ id_ed25519.pub   │  or HTTPS+token │ + Git objects    │
 └──────────────────┘                 └──────────────────┘
         git push / git fetch
```

## SSH keys

Generate an **ed25519** key if you do not have one:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ada@example.com" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

Press Enter for no passphrase, or set one (then `ssh-agent` remembers it for the session):

```bash
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

Public key (this is what you paste into the forge):

```bash
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

The private file `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` stays on your machine. Never commit it. Never paste it into a ticket.

On the forge: account settings → SSH keys → paste the `.pub` line. GitHub, GitLab, and Forgejo all have this screen. The label can be `laptop`.

Test (GitHub as an example host; use your forge’s hostname):

```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```

A greeting that includes your username means the key was accepted. A password prompt means the server did not see the key (`ssh -v` shows which files it tried).

`~/.ssh/config` for several hosts:

```text
Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Host forgejo.home
  HostName 192.168.68.200
  User git
  Port 2222
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

A later Forgejo lab uses a port like 2222. The `Host` alias lets you write `git@forgejo.home:ada/desk-api.git`.

## HTTPS and tokens

```bash
git clone https://github.com/example/desk-api.git
```

Pushing over HTTPS asks for a username and a **personal access token** (not your account password on most forges). Store it in a credential helper:

```bash
git config --global credential.helper libsecret   # GNOME Keyring / libsecret, if installed
# memory-only fallback (forgets at reboot or after a timeout):
git config --global credential.helper cache
```

CI systems often use HTTPS with a job-scoped token. Humans on a laptop usually have an easier time with SSH.

## Pick one default

For this book’s desk repos on a machine you own: **SSH**. Clone and remote URLs will look like:

```text
git@host:owner/desk-api.git
```

You can change a remote later (chapter 11):

```bash
git remote -v
git remote set-url origin git@host:owner/desk-api.git
```

Chapter 3 stays local: `git init` does not need SSH or HTTPS.
